subject: dwarfRifleman
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf rifleman with braided beard and blunderbuss.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but rich Warcraft-style dwarf rifleman model—chunky proportions, big pauldrons, braided beard, and a flared blunderbuss—keeping the scale around 1.3 m tall and using the SDK API carefully to avoid errors.

For the pose, I'm going with a slight A-pose with arms extended outward, gun held in the right hand angled forward-down and attached to the wrist bone. I'm sketching out the skeleton hierarchy—hips rooted low, a spine chain running hips to chest to neck to head, and arm chains with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints—while working out the model-space coordinates for each joint along the spine and arms.

Now I'm extending this into the neck and head joints, adding a jaw joint parented to the head, and sizing the head larger to fit a dwarf proportions. Then I'm defining torso loft stations along the spine bone with varying widths and heights to shape the vest-like torso, keeping the color palette simple and limited, and starting to plan out the leg geometry next.

Still building boot geometry...

Now I'm setting up the arm chain with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints positioned to create a natural bent arm pose.

Adding the gun pointing diagonally forward-down from the right hand, with a stock, barrel, flared muzzle cone, and brass bands built along that gun axis direction.

For the figure itself, I'm naming the arm joints shoulder/elbow/hand per side, leaving the left hand empty but maybe adding a powder horn on the belt. For the head, I'm building a skull sphere with a bulbous nose, brow boxes, and simple sphere eyes with pupils, positioning everything relative to a head center point.

I'm adding ginger-red hair and brows, pointed ears, a hidden jaw bone, and a beard setup with mustache capsules and braided chin hair made of bead-like spheres strung along curved paths with gold ring ends.

Still refining the braid path logic and bone attachment, then switching to a swept polyline shape for the beard's main mass tapering from chin to chest.

For hairstyle details, I'm planning two braided strands with gold clasps and tufted cone ends, then moving on to headgear — a dwarf rifleman cap with a domed lathe shape, brim, band, and a feather accent.

I'm positioning the hat brim just above the brows at eye level, sizing it to sit properly above the head mesh, and now working out the belt geometry as a swept elliptical ring around the waist matching the torso's tapered loft dimensions at the hips.

I'm refining the torso loft stations with specific width/depth values at each height, placing a gold buckle box at the front of the belt, and now sketching the bandolier as a diagonal sweep across the chest.

Switching to a simpler rod geometry from left shoulder to right hip for the bandolier, with small cartridge pouches lerped along its length. Then I'm thinking through textures needed, including a gryphon-like emblem decal to place on a chest tabard plane.

I'll pull metal paints (steel, brass, gilt, iron) from the clockwork kit rather than glow effects, and build plaid trousers by nesting crossed stripe patterns for a woven look.

Now I'm laying out the gun: stock positioned behind the gripping hand, lock at the base, a brass-banded barrel extending forward, and a flared muzzle built from a tapered cylinder for the wide-mouthed blunderbuss shape.

Positioning hands and fingers...

Now I'm adding the pauldron: a dome sphere with a gold ring torus around the shoulder, plus a scattering of rivet-like studs placed via trig around the dome edge.

Next I'm building the collar/gorget as a flattened torus at the neck, then assembling boots with ankle cuffs, a boxy boot shape, and a dark sole plate, before starting on the leg sweep geometry from the hip joint.

Placing the head at the top with skull radius slightly overlapping the torso's top, keeping the neck short for a dwarf proportion. For the torso I'm using a loft along the spine chain with sections oriented by the path tangent, then moving on to figure out how the arms attach at the shoulder.

Now I'm designing a lathe profile for the hat brim and crown, tracing an outline that goes out along the bottom, up through the brim edge, and back in toward the axis without crossing itself, then positioning the hat so it sits just below the head's top to cover the skull.

Adding a brass hat band and a feather extrusion on the back side of the hat, working out the outline points and axis directions for the feather shape.

Now I'm placing small ear cones on each side angled outward and upward, plus mustache capsules curling from the corners of the mouth.

For the beard, I'm sweeping a tapered tube down the chin with a radius function that narrows toward the bottom, tinted with a darker hair grain texture, and tying it to the jaw bone so it opens along with the jaw. Then I'm starting on braid geometry next.

Good, locking in a bedroll backpack for a dwarf-style character. For the rig I'm setting hips as root with the spine chain parented off it, and I'm defining a helper function to place body parts by bone, position, color, and rotation, keeping the color palette compact. For the emblem texture I'm sketching an SVG shield decal with a blue fill, gold border, and crossed hammer motif, clipped to the shield outline.

I'm deciding to keep just two textures plus procedural paints rather than adding more decals like a rune or buckle, since that's enough given the effort budget. I'm applying a surface decal onto the torso sweep at a point near the chest, projecting along the forward direction, and adding a skin mottle paint effect to the head and hands for texture variation.

Now I'm working out joint positions for the arms using three-point catmull paths from shoulder to elbow to wrist, then placing the gun at the hand position with a slight inward barrel angle so it points toward center rather than straight forward.

I'm figuring out the right offset so the gun barrel clears the floor, then setting up the lathe and box part signatures with direction and axis options, and making sure to reference the spine's tip joint correctly before exporting the final result.
